title: NaturalReader Pricing 2026: Plans, Costs & Comparison
summary: NaturalReader pricing offers free and paid plans with different voice options and usage limits. Compare tiers to find what suits your needs.
body_markdown:
## Hidden costs and limits NaturalReader users hit


If the fine print blocks your work, the savings from moving up a plan vanish. Five limits can: commercial rights, MP3 export allowance, tier-gated voices, the annual commitment, and renewal and refund terms. I confirmed only the prices; I flagged each other item.


I couldn't verify commercial-use rights beyond the plan names, so read the licence text before publishing paid work. I found no confirmed MP3 export cap, and I couldn't confirm which voices sit on Starter versus Creator.


If you publish audio for clients or monetised channels, personal-tier pricing is the wrong comparison. The plans page lists Starter and Creator under its commercial plans. I couldn't verify the licence wording, so confirm it covers your use before you pay.


If you batch-export audiobook chapters or course narration, ask support for the monthly allowance before relying on a plan.


If those chapters arrive as documents someone has to feed into a TTS step by hand, Activepieces, which has 750 integrations, can take over that routing, and that is all it speaks to: it doesn't tell you which NaturalReader plan to buy.


Describe the process in its built-in chat (a new article arrives, its text goes to your TTS service, the audio lands in a folder) and what comes back is a live flow in your account, with a run trace showing what happened at each step.


Flows are unlimited on every plan, including free, so testing the build costs nothing.


### NaturalReader annual billing versus monthly pricing


If you take Starter, it's[$29 a month, or $16.50 a month billed annually](https://www.naturalreaders.com/payment/commpay/plans) . Over twelve months that's $348 against $198, so annual saves $150 but commits you for the year.


On Creator it's $49 monthly or $24.75 annually. That's $588 against $297, so annual saves $291. If NaturalReader charges the annual price as one payment, which I couldn't verify, you'd put $297 down on Creator before testing it on real work.


So annual billing is worth it only once you've confirmed your voice and licence needs on a monthly month.


Before paying annually, check whether the plan auto-renews and whether unused months are refundable.
